prompt.context: You are a consultant who has been engaged by "Sunshine Power", owner of a coal power station on the Sunshine Coast of Australia. 6 years ago Sunshine Power commenced a pilot project with "SunSteam", a solar tech company. SunSteam technology allows your client to reduce the quantity of coal it consumes by using sunlight as an additional heat source. The $3.5M AUD pilot, involving one SunSteam array, experienced many technical difficulties at first but has just broken even. Recently, SunSteam proposed to expand the pilot by constructing four additional SunSteam arrays. Your client has very specific project investment criteria and is not sure if they should accept the SunSteam proposal.
prompt.question: Should Sunshine Power accept SunSteam's proposal to expand the pilot by constructing four additional SunSteam arrays? The client's investment criteria requires payback in less than 5 years, based on internal cost savings only.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost of the expansion?
clarifying_info.a: Unknown – assume $3.5M AUD per array, same as the pilot, so $14M AUD total for four arrays.

clarifying_info.q: What is the output of one SunSteam array?
clarifying_info.a: Steam produced by one array equates to a 0.2% saving in annual coal quantity consumed on average.

clarifying_info.q: What is the plant's annual coal consumption?
clarifying_info.a: The plant operates 24 hours a day at 100% output capacity. Prior to the pilot it consumed 4 million metric tons of thermal coal per annum.

clarifying_info.q: What are the operating costs of the arrays?
clarifying_info.a: SunSteam is easy to maintain and is maintained by existing on-site staff. Assume operating cost = $0.

clarifying_info.q: What are the client's investment criteria?
clarifying_info.a: Payback must be less than 5 years, based on internal cost savings only.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of coal?
clarifying_info.a: See Exhibit 3 – Spot Price of Thermal Coal over the last 5 years (provided only when asked).

exhibits.title: Sunshine Power Station Site Plan
exhibits.shows: A simple sketch of the Sunshine Power Station site showing the current layout and proposed plans for the expansion of SunSteam arrays.
exhibits.data: Site layout with existing pilot array and space for four additional arrays.

exhibits.title: SunSteam Technology Flow Chart
exhibits.shows: A flow chart illustrating how SunSteam technology works, showing inputs and outputs of the system.
exhibits.data: Inputs: sunlight, water. Process: mirrors focus sunlight to boil water and create steam. Output: steam fed into the existing coal power plant boiler cycle, reducing coal required.

exhibits.title: Spot Price of Thermal Coal (Last 5 Years)
exhibits.shows: A chart of the spot price of thermal coal over the last 5 years (provided only when candidate asks about the cost or price of coal).
exhibits.data: Approximately 5 years of price data; current price approximately $83 AUD per metric ton; price was higher in prior years (above $87.50 for most of the period) and has declined in recent years.

framework: Define the investment decision: compare total fixed cost of expansion to cumulative cost savings within 5-year payback window
Quantify fixed investment: 4 arrays x $3.5M AUD = $14M AUD total
Quantify coal savings volume: 4 arrays x 0.2% = 0.8% saving; 0.8% x 4,000,000 MT = 32,000 MT per year
Calculate break-even coal price needed to meet payback criteria: $14M / (32,000 MT x 5 yr) = $87.50/MT
Compare break-even price to current and historical coal prices using Exhibit 3
Assess risks and benefits; form recommendation

questions.prompt: Calculate the total fixed investment cost for the four-array expansion.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognise that no cost is given for the expansion and must make an assumption based on the pilot. Cost per array = $3.5M AUD (same as pilot). Four arrays = 4 x $3.5M = $14M AUD.

math.setup: Cost per array (assumed from pilot) x number of new arrays
steps: $3.5M AUD per array x 4 arrays = $14M AUD

questions.prompt: How much coal will be saved annually if all four new arrays are installed?
questions.guidance: One array saves 0.2% of annual coal consumption. Four arrays save 0.8%. Annual base consumption = 4,000,000 MT. Candidate may use the shortcut of calculating 0.1% then doubling three times.

math.setup: (Number of arrays x savings per array) x annual coal consumption
math.answer: 32,000 metric tons of coal saved per year

questions.prompt: What is the break-even price of coal required for the project to meet the 5-year payback criterion?
questions.guidance: Two equivalent approaches are valid. Approach 1: spread fixed cost over 5 years ($14M / 5 = $2.8M/yr), then divide by annual tonnage saved ($2.8M / 32,000 = $87.50/MT). Approach 2: total cost divided by total tonnes saved over 5 years ($14M / 160,000 = $87.50/MT). Candidate can also pick a coal price from Exhibit 3 and verify positive or negative return.

math.setup: Break-even price = Total fixed investment / (Annual coal saving x Payback period in years)
steps: Annual fixed cost amortised: $14,000,000 / 5 = $2,800,000 per year
math.answer: $87.50 AUD per metric ton is the break-even coal price

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 3, does the current coal price support the investment?
questions.guidance: Current spot price is approximately $83/MT, which is below the $87.50 break-even. At $83 the project does NOT meet the 5-year payback criterion. However, for most of the past 5 years prices were above $87.50, so if prices recover the project would meet criteria. Strong candidates note the declining trend and question whether prices will rebound.

math.answer: At $83/MT the project misses payback criteria by ~$144,000/year; payback would take approximately 5.3 years

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the core payback calculation, what are the broader risks and benefits of proceeding with the SunSteam expansion?

categories.name: Benefits
ideas: Sunlight is free – zero fuel cost for energy from solar arrays
Reduces carbon emissions, potentially generating carbon credits or tax exemptions
Corporate social responsibility / sustainability branding benefits
Proven technology from pilot reduces technical risk for future arrays
If coal prices rise above $87.50 on average, payback criteria is met with meaningful savings
Coal consumption can be reduced further if additional arrays are added in future

categories.name: Risks
ideas: Coal price volatility: lower prices mean slower or no payback (currently $83 < $87.50 break-even)
Technical difficulties similar to the pilot could delay payback
Plant operates 24 hours; sunlight is only available ~50% of the time (daytime), capping maximum coal reduction at around 50%
Construction cost overruns could push break-even price higher
SunSteam as a supplier risk: dependency on single vendor for maintenance and future supply

categories.name: Next Steps
ideas: Hedge or lock in coal price via futures or option contracts to mitigate price volatility risk
Negotiate down construction cost; at $3.3M per array instead of $3.5M the project meets criteria at current $83 coal price
Conduct technical due diligence on causes of pilot difficulties to size probability of recurrence
Explore carbon credit monetisation to supplement cost savings
Revisit inclusion of original pilot array in payback calculation (if included, savings = 1% or 40,000 MT/yr, lowering break-even price)

recommendation: Do NOT accept the proposal at current coal prices – the break-even price of $87.50/MT exceeds the current spot price of ~$83/MT, meaning the 5-year payback criterion is not met under today's market conditions.

However, the decision is price-sensitive: coal traded above $87.50 for most of the prior 5 years. If prices are expected to recover above $87.50 on average over the next 5 years, the project does meet payback criteria and should be approved.
risks: Coal price could remain depressed or fall further, extending payback beyond 5 years
Technical difficulties (as experienced in the pilot) could further delay payback
Sunlight availability limits maximum coal savings to ~50%, capping long-term upside
next_steps: Mitigate coal price risk by hedging or locking in an option contract above $87.50
Negotiate construction cost down to approximately $3.3M per array, which would allow the project to meet payback criteria at the current $83 coal price
Quantify potential carbon credit and tax benefits to determine if they can bridge the current ~$4.50/MT gap
Conduct technical review of pilot difficulties before committing to four-array expansion
